literal: Like those who have nothing before those who possess, even standing in eager humility, those who learned; the lowest indeed are those who have not learned.
translation: Those who acquire learning by standing in eager humility before their teacher, like the destitute standing before the wealthy, are the truly learned; those who do not learn thus are indeed the lowest.
modern: செல்வம் உடையவர்களின் முன் வறியவர்கள் இரந்து நிற்பது போல, பணிந்து நின்று ஏங்கித் தவித்துக் கற்றவர்களே சிறந்தவர்கள்; அவ்வாறு செய்ய நாணி கல்லாதவர் எக்காலத்திலும் கடைப்பட்டவரே ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the necessity of humility in the pursuit of knowledge. The poet compares a student seeking knowledge to a poor person standing expectantly before a wealthy benefactor. Those who are willing to humble themselves and show an eager desire to learn are the ones who become truly educated. Conversely, those who are too proud to adopt this humble posture of learning remain ignorant and are deemed the lowest in society.
